summary: Kennard Lipman is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed doctoral studies under Herbert V. Guenther (attested 1979). He has served as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

Kenneth Ballhatchet (1922–1995) was a historian and Indologist who studied at Clifton College and Peterhouse, Cambridge. He served as Reader in Indian History at the University of Oxford (1963–1965) and taught at SOAS University of London (1948–1988).
Kenneth Doo Young Lee specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University (attested 2007).

Kenneth G. Zysk (born 1951) is an Indologist and historian. He earned an M.A. from UC Santa Barbara and a Ph.D. from Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later serving at Eastern Michigan University and the University of Copenhagen.

Kenneth J. Guest is a scholar of religious studies and Sinology. He studied at Columbia, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, and the CUNY Graduate Center under Aloysius Pieris, and has held posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a Buddhist studies and religion scholar educated at Emmanuel College and under W. D. C. Wagiswara. He served at Trinity College (1908–1912), YMCA College (1913), Pacific School of Religion (1921), and UC (~1921–1935).

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar. He was a professor at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999) and chaired both the Numata Center (1996–1999) and Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai (until 1999).

Kenneth K. S. Ch'en (1907–1993) was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Hawaiʻi, Yenching, and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. His posts included Harvard, UCLA (1958–1961, 1971–1976), and Princeton University (1961–1971).

Kenneth K. Tanaka (born 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees from Stanford and UC Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini. He held faculty posts at the Institute of Buddhist Studies and Musashino University.

Kenneth R. Valpey (born 1950) works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and has held a post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenneth Somerled Macdonald (1832–1903) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who was educated at the University of Aberdeen and Free Church College. He served with the United Free Church Mission (~1862–1903) and the University of Calcutta.

Kenneth W. Jones (1934–1996) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Stockton University and UC Berkeley under Thomas Metcalf, and spent his career teaching at Kansas State University from 1965, becoming Distinguished Professor in 1989.

Kenryo Minowa (born 1960) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo. He has held faculty positions at Aichi Gakuin University, the University of Tokyo, and Rissho University.

Kenryu Nishio (born 1948) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He received his doctorate from Otani University and became Professor Emeritus at Hanazono University (attested 2014, 2026).
Kenryu Tsuji (1919–2004) was a Buddhist studies scholar who pursued his education at Ryukoku University (1938) and the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Bukkyo University. He was a professor at Koyasan, Seizan, and Shuchiin universities, and was named professor emeritus at Ryukoku University in 1956.
Kenshi Kusano (born 1952) specializes in Buddhist studies, history, and Japanology. He studied at Otani University, where he also held a professorship (attested 2006).

Kenta Suzuki (born 1975) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and the University of Tokyo. He held an associate professorship at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 2015–2016).

Kenyu Mitomo (born 1945) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who earned master's and doctoral degrees at Rissho University. He served Rissho University from 1968 to 2015, notably as Dean of the Faculty of Buddhist Studies.

Kevin A. Vose is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He earned degrees from Bates College and the University of Virginia, studying under traditional teacher Khen Rinpoche Ngawang Jinpa and doctoral supervisor Jeffrey Hopkins.
